answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making reputation costly to harvest and cheap to verify. Like saffron, which takes thousands of flowers for one gram, trust should grow only from a long sequence of verifiable useful tasks, published to a public mirror ledger. New identities start with no privileges and earn them slowly, so creating thousands of fakes means redoing that costly history each time. An oasis of free, instant trust is what attackers exploit; remove it, and grant no reputation without proven work.
